source.title: Trainable Weight Averaging for Fast Convergence and Better Generalization
source.authors: Tao Li; Zhehao Huang; Qing-Hua Tao; Ying-Wen Wu; X. Huang

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no truncation or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how trainable weight averaging affects train/test generalization gaps on natural-data tasks, extending the claim’s subject to a weight-averaging method. It does not test the listed version-specific claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports generalization-gap results for TWA on CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and WMT2014. Results about test accuracy without a reported gap, and comparisons cited from other work, are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates trainable weight averaging, not any of V1–V8. Generalization gaps alone do not test these specific claims. Different optimizers are used for different architectures without a controlled optimizer comparison; batch size and dropout are not experimentally varied. Large-batch work is cited as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that learning weight-averaging coefficients improves performance and training efficiency, with validation-supervised TWA-v particularly effective. They also acknowledge sensitivity to checkpoint selection, restriction to a single linear mode, and remaining overfitting risk.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces trainable weight averaging over historical or fine-tuned checkpoints, optimizing coefficients in a subspace. It does not use the random-label memorization, width-sweep, architecture comparison, optimizer comparison, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-measurement, or memorized-example-removal recipes in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies by architecture, dataset, and coefficient-optimization data (training versus validation). The authors also state that selecting historical solutions can influence performance.

fits_no_version.finding: TWA improves held-out performance with fewer training epochs or steps and lowers reported signed training–test gaps. Validation-supervised TWA-v generally improves on TWA-t. For ImageNet ResNets, lower signed gaps do not mean smaller absolute gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing averaging coefficients over historical checkpoints can improve held-out performance and training efficiency, with results depending on architecture and coefficient-training data.

record.problems: The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported generalization gaps. CIFAR results use three random seeds and report standard deviations for test accuracy, but not for the gaps. Table 4's flattened layout makes gap-to-method assignment ambiguous; corresponding row values are flagged. The study does not test random-label memorization or the specific mechanisms in the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly reported generalization-gap results were omitted. Accuracy-only tables and cited results were excluded because they do not report the gap measure relevant to the extracted finding.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization with the same recipe, and chance-level held-out random-label accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and the effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison against norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to V1–V8; cannot_determine describes their inability to establish a listed version, not unreadability of every number. Table 4 has no SWA gap column; its two post-SWA gap columns belong to TWA-t and TWA-v. Accuracy-only results elsewhere do not supply missing tests of the listed versions. The recorded rows are method-performance comparisons and should not be treated as claim evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; chance performance on held-out random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior around the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, local connectivity, and learned sparse connections.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and effects of changing training recipes.
Dropout effects, underfitting from excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measured network properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
